business_problem: Tata Projects had to review 1,000-2,000 page tender packages with non-standard terms, scanned tables, and frequent corrigenda, so manual analysis took more than four days per bid and made it difficult to spot risk and respond quickly enough to stay competitive.
solution_summary: Tata Projects and TCS built TenderSummAIze, a generative AI tender-management portal on Microsoft Azure that turns bulky infrastructure bid documents into structured, searchable working material for legal and contracts teams. Tender files and scanned pages are processed with Document Intelligence and Microsoft Azure OpenAI so the system can chunk clauses semantically, map corrigenda back to the original document set, answer tender questions, and generate tailored summaries. Microsoft Azure Durable Functions orchestrates the long-running workflow, while Cosmos DB and Microsoft Azure Queue hold state and scale data movement across the pipeline. The portal lets teams upload, review, query, summarize, and track tenders through one interface, replacing reactive document reading with a governed AI workflow that surfaces liabilities and key terms in time for faster bid decisions.

data_flow: Tender documents, scanned pages, and corrigenda are uploaded into TenderSummAIze, where Document Intelligence extracts content and Microsoft Azure OpenAI organizes clauses, highlights liabilities, answers questions, and produces summaries. Durable Functions and Azure Queue orchestrate the long-running steps, Cosmos DB maintains the working state and document lineage, and legal and contracts teams consume the results through the portal for faster bid decisions.
business_outcome: TenderSummAIze gave Tata Projects a faster and more reliable bid-preparation workflow, reducing manual review time, increasing accuracy, and helping the company evaluate more tenders with the same teams while shifting effort from clerical document handling to strategic commercial analysis.
